key_idea: Compute all-pairs shortest paths, then build a second graph on the 'refill' nodes (school, stations, home) with an edge only when the shortest distance is at most d, and run shortest paths again.
sketch: Floyd-Warshall on the n<=500 intersections (1.25e8 simple operations) gives dist. Take the key nodes {1, stations, n}; connect two of them with weight dist if dist <= d, else infinity. A second Floyd-Warshall (or Dijkstra) on this graph gives the answer from school to home, or 'stuck' if unreachable. Use 64-bit distances since edge weights are up to 2^31 and sums overflow int; skip rows with infinite pivot distance to avoid overflow. Arriving exactly when the tire goes flat is allowed, so the comparison is <= d.
